not_found: 882 nm cooling line: isotope shifts for the nine stable isotopes and the 131Xe (and 129Xe) hyperfine constants of 6p[5/2]3 measured in a MOT by Walhout, Megens, Witte, Rolston (Phys. Rev. A 48, R879 (1993)) - only the abstract (no numbers) could be opened; no other open source for A, B of 6p[5/2]3 was found (Husson, Grandin, Kucal, J. Physique 40, 551 (1979), HAL jpa-00209138, is behind a bot wall).
823 nm line isotope shifts (D'Amico et al. 1999): abstract only, no numbers; the 841.15 and 820.86 nm shifts of Bounds et al. are recorded instead.
Absolute optical frequencies of 882 / 823 nm better than NIST: not located.
Directly measured lifetime of 6p[5/2]3 and A values newer than NIST: 33.03 ns is the Vassen-review table value.

Measured Lande g factors beyond NIST ASD: Huet et al. (J. Physique 40, 541 (1979)) covers 6s[3/2]1, 6p'[3/2]1 and 7p levels but the PDF could not be opened; NIST ASD already lists g for the levels drawn.
Experimental reduced matrix elements: none located.

Lifetime of 129Xe / 131Xe 3P2 (hyperfine-quenched): the Walhout abstract states it is much shorter in 129Xe but gives no number. The 6s'[1/2]0 clock-state decay rate is now stored from the Opt. Lett. abstract.

Level-resolved radiative lifetimes of the 6p, 6p', 7p, 6d levels: Inoue, Ku, Setser (J. Chem. Phys. 81, 5760 (1984)) abstract gives only ranges (30-48 ns for 6p and 6p', 68-172 ns for 7p); Bruce et al. (J. Chem. Phys. 92, 2917 (1990)) and Boewering et al. (84, 715 (1986)) abstracts carry no numbers; full texts are paywalled. Suzuki & Shimoda (J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 43, 1977; OSTI abstract) give 35 +- 2 ns and 37 +- 4 ns for levels written '6p22' and '6p01' and 520 +- 30 ns for '5d33'; the notation could not be mapped to NIST levels with certainty, so they were not stored.

Two-photon laser-induced-fluorescence (TALIF) lines of Xe (224.3 / 225.5 nm schemes) with measured lifetimes: the open-access review (Eur. Phys. J. Techn. Instrum. 2022) is behind a bot wall; no annotation added.
Interferometric 6s[3/2]2-6s'[1/2]0 clock frequency (Opt. Lett. 20, 1421 (1995)): not opened.
AFIT thesis 'Investigation of Metastable Xenon' (129Xe hyperfine coefficient of 6p[5/2]3 at 882 nm) blocked for automated access.
conflicts: 131Xe B(6s[3/2]2): D'Amico et al. 255.7(0.6) MHz vs Bounds et al. 246.7(2) MHz (823 nm) and 259(7) MHz (841 nm); A(131) 705.4(0.4) vs 708.3(1) MHz. The D'Amico values, consistent with the atomic-beam intervals of Faust & McDermott (|A129| = 2384.50 MHz derived), are used.
129Xe A(6s'[1/2]1): D'Amico -5808(2) MHz vs Bounds -5782(4) / -5785(2) MHz (about 25 MHz apart).
3P2 lifetime 42.9(9) s (Walhout 1994) is less than half of the theoretical values (96-150 s); no competing measurement.

6s'[1/2]0 lifetime: measured spontaneous rate 7.8(38) s^-1 (0.128 s, 49 % uncertainty) vs theory 0.078 s (12.8 s^-1), 1.3 sigma apart; the effective room-temperature lifetime is 13.3 ms because of blackbody-induced deexcitation.
8s[3/2]1 energy: Ramsey-comb value for 132Xe 90932.44142 cm^-1 vs NIST 90932.432 cm^-1 (natural mixture), 0.009 cm^-1 apart.

Brandi et al. 2001 calibrated energies (136Xe 8d[1/2]1 94228.0187, 8d[3/2]1 94685.4822; 132Xe 7s'[1/2]1 95800.5867 cm^-1) lie 0.003-0.015 cm^-1 above the NIST values; the measurement is older than 20 years, so NIST stays in use.
notes: Hyperfine entries taken from the comparison table of Bounds et al. are second-hand (method 'compilation', original named in the source); Bounds' own results are listed as alternatives. Isotope-shift keys are kept exactly as printed (pair label 'A-B' with a negative value); see each note on the unverified sign convention. Values converted from mK carry the printed mK numbers alongside. Level energies are NIST ASD values from data/xe/levels.csv; Paschen names in the labels. Entries marked '(abstract)' were read on the publisher's abstract page or HAL record only. Added 2026-10-01 (second pass): VUV isotope shifts of Brandi et al. are printed as nu(136) - nu(A) (positive = lighter isotope at lower frequency); Dreissen et al. print nu(A) - nu(132).
